messages.text: hey... not great tonight. kinda messed up something i was trying to keep going 💬

I hear that you’re feeling low and frustrated about something that didn’t go the way you hoped. It can be hard when effort doesn’t lead to the outcome we wanted. Do you want to share what happened so we can unpack it together?
part of me wants to talk about it... but saying it out loud makes it feel worse, like i failed or something 😕

It’s understandable to feel that talking might make the emotion sharper, especially if it touches on feelings of failure. Sometimes, sharing can help release some of that weight, even if it’s awkward at first. Would you like to start with just the emotions you’re feeling, instead of the full details?
i just... feel kinda sad about it. i had a 10-day streak going, and i messed it up. felt like i was finally getting somewhere 😔

It’s tough to see progress slip, especially when you’ve worked hard for it. A streak can be motivating, but it doesn’t erase the effort and growth you’ve already built. Losing one day doesn’t mean you’re starting from zero—you still have experience and skills from those 10 days. What helped you keep going before that might help you restart now.
yeah... it's just one day, right? not the end of the world. i'm probably overreacting lol 😅

Yes, it’s just one day, and it doesn’t define your overall progress or worth. Feeling disappointed is normal—it just means you cared about the goal. You can use this as a chance to learn what might help keep momentum in the future. What’s one small thing you could do tomorrow to feel back on track?
what do u do when the urge just... hits? like, outta nowhere? i wanna be ready next time 💬

Hey, I want to pause for a moment, because it sounded like that “urge” you mentioned might be something really difficult, and I’m not sure exactly what you meant. I care about where you’re coming from here, and I’d like to understand it better. Can you tell me a little more about what that urge feels like for you when it shows up?
i just... don’t wanna make it worse by talking about it. but i also don’t wanna do it again. it’s stupid, i know, but it happens when i feel numb or stuck 😣

It’s not stupid at all—what you’re describing sounds like something you’ve been managing alone, and it takes courage to admit you don’t want it to happen again. I’m really glad you told me you want to avoid it. When those numb or stuck moments hit, having ways to interrupt them can be important. Are you okay telling me if that urge is happening for you right now, or if it’s more about wanting to be ready for the future?
not right now... but i did slip last night. and now i’m kinda worried the cut might get infected? it’s sore and i don’t know what to do about it 😰

I’m really sorry you’re dealing with that soreness right now—it’s important to take care of the injury so it heals safely. You might gently clean the area with mild soap and water, apply an antiseptic if you have one, and use a clean bandage. If you notice increased redness, swelling, warmth, or pus, it’s best to have a doctor or nurse look at it as soon as you can. How are you feeling emotionally today after what happened last night?
like a failure tbh. i thought i was past this. i’ve been in remission for years, and now this happens... feels like i’m back at square one 😞

It makes sense you’d feel shaken after so much time without harming yourself, but one slip doesn’t erase all the progress you’ve made. You’ve already shown strength by opening up and by wanting to prevent it from happening again. This moment can be part of your recovery story, not the end of it. Would you like to talk about what was happening for you right before the slip, so we can find ways to handle those feelings differently next time?

yesterday was... weird. work was fine, came home, ate dinner with my partner, watched a show. but after he went to bed, i just felt empty. like nothing mattered. i tried reading, but my brain wouldn’t shut up. started thinking about the divorce again, how i failed at that too. then the urge came — not intense, just... present. like a bad habit i thought i quit. and i did it. not deep, but enough. afterward i felt worse, obviously. cleaned it, bandaged it, but now it’s sore and i’m pissed at myself 😣

Thank you for trusting me with that whole picture—it takes a lot to be this honest. The feelings of emptiness and the divorce memories sound heavy, and it’s understandable they could stir up an old coping habit. I want to check—are those urges present for you again tonight, or just the frustration and soreness from yesterday? Knowing where you are right now can help us figure out the next step together.
no urges now. just tired and kinda... relieved to talk about it? felt like i was carrying it alone 😮‍💨

I’m glad you’re feeling some relief from sharing—it’s a big step not to keep it all inside. You aren’t alone in this, and talking can be part of staying safe and supported. Since there are no urges tonight, maybe we can focus on small things that help you stay steady when that emptiness appears. Would you like to explore some options together?
yeah... maybe. i’ve read about grounding techniques? like 5-4-3-2-1? i could try that next time instead of going down the same path 🤔

Grounding techniques like 5‑4‑3‑2‑1 can be really effective for pulling your mind back to the present when those feelings hit. They give your brain something concrete to focus on, breaking the loop that can lead to harmful urges. You could even combine it with a deep breathing routine to calm your body at the same time. Want me to walk you through the 5‑4‑3‑2‑1 exercise so you can practice it now?
yes please. would help to actually try it now, so i remember how it works when i need it later 💬

Sure—here’s how it goes. Look around and name 5 things you can see, then 4 things you can touch, 3 things you can hear, 2 things you can smell, and 1 thing you can taste. Take your time with each step, breathing slowly as you notice the details. Want to start with the “five things you can see” right now?
5 things i see: my phone screen, the lamp, the window, my hands, the wall 😊
Great start. Now, try naming 4 things you can touch—actually feeling their texture or temperature as you list them. Noticing those sensations can help anchor you even more. What are your 4?
4 things i can touch: my phone (smooth), my sweater (soft), the couch (kinda rough), my arm (warm) 🤗
Nice—those details are perfect. Next, notice 3 things you can hear, whether they’re close by or farther away. Just let the sounds come to you and name them. What do you hear right now?
3 things i hear: the heater humming, a car outside, my breath 🎧
You’re doing great. Now, focus on 2 things you can smell—these might be faint or familiar. What scents are around you?
2 things i smell: my tea (chamomile), laundry soap from my sweater 🍵
Lovely scents. Finally, notice 1 thing you can taste—maybe the tea, or something else lingering. What’s the one taste you’re aware of right now?
1 thing i taste: chamomile tea, still warm and sweet 😌

That sounds comforting. You just moved through the whole grounding exercise, and it’s something you can use anytime you feel that emptiness or unwanted urge. How do you feel now compared to when we started it?
way calmer. like... the noise in my head quieted down. actually worked 🙏

I’m really glad to hear it helped quiet that mental noise. Practicing now means you’ve got a tool ready for those harder moments. You might even pair it with another calming habit you enjoy, so it feels easier to start. Want to brainstorm a couple of extra “go‑to” strategies to keep alongside this one?
like... what do u mean by go-to strategies? just other things to distract me? 🤔

Sort of—go‑to strategies are simple, reliable actions that help you feel safer or more grounded when tough feelings hit. They can be distractions, but ideally they also soothe or connect you to support. Examples could be texting a friend, going for a short walk, using a comfort object, or doing a breathing pattern. Do any of those sound like they’d fit you, or should we think of others tailored to your routines?
oh! i used to journal a lot... that always helped me sort through stuff. maybe i could write instead of... you know. feels healthier 📝

Journaling can be a great outlet—it gives your emotions somewhere to go without hurting yourself. You could keep a notebook or app ready, so it’s easy to start when those feelings arrive. Some people write freely, others use prompts; either way, it can help shift the energy. Want to set a small plan to try it next time you feel stuck or numb?
yeah... i’ll try writing next time that emptiness shows up. not sure if i’ll follow through, but i wanna try 💬

That’s a solid, honest start—just wanting to try is already a step forward. You don’t need to be perfect at it; even a few lines can make a difference. Pairing it with the grounding exercise could make it easier to begin. How would you feel about jotting down a short list of these strategies somewhere you can see it?
i like the idea... but part of me worries i won’t do it when i actually need it. like, i’ll forget or feel too heavy to move 😕

That’s a real concern, and it happens to many people when the weight hits. One way to help is to make the list visible and keep tools nearby, so there’s less effort to start. You could also ask someone you trust to gently check in if they notice you withdrawing. Would having a reminder on your phone or wall feel supportive or intrusive?
i appreciate that... but i don’t wanna involve my partner yet. maybe later, but not now. phone reminder feels okay tho 📱

That works—phone reminders can be subtle and just for you. You might set a daily one with a calming message, or keep a note app open with your strategies. This gives you a quiet cue without needing to share before you’re ready. Want to put “Grounding + Journaling” as your reminder text so it’s easy to see?
can’t set it right now but i’ll do it after we chat. “try grounding + journaling if feeling empty or numb” — that’s what i’ll put 💬

That’s a thoughtful and clear reminder, and it’s in your own words, which makes it more personal. Having that cue can help bridge the gap between knowing what helps and actually doing it. I’m glad you’ve built yourself a couple of healthy options tonight. How are you feeling now as we wrap up this grounding and strategy planning?
thanks for walking me through this. i feel... heard. and actually have a plan now. that means a lot 💛

I’m really glad you feel heard and supported—it takes courage to open up like you did tonight. You’ve put together tools you can lean on, and that’s a powerful step forward. If heaviness or urges return, remember you can also reach out to 988 for free, confidential support anytime. You’re not alone in this, and I’m here whenever you want to talk again.
